licence.name: Class 5 driver's licence (full class licence, after the Graduated Driver Licensing Program)

note: Read 2026-10-31 in archive.org's snapshot of 13 November 2025 of Yukon's own page 'Get a driver's licence' (saved 2026-10-31 by wave 16; yukon.ca answers this egress 403 with a Cloudflare challenge today, and archive.org's CDX reset every connection today, so no later snapshot was looked up). New drivers complete the Graduated Driver Licensing Program: a learner's licence from 15; the road test from at least 16, after 6 months on the learner's licence, gives a novice licence; at least 18 months in the novice stage before a full class licence. The youngest full holder is so 17 years and 6 months, 16 plus the novice stage's 18 months, my arithmetic from the page's stages. The page gives no fee or term for the full licence (only the $20 written and road tests, not held), so both are null; a search snippet of the renewal page ($100 for five years) wasn't read and isn't used. Yukon's identification card wasn't read. Until 2026-10-31 Yukon stood blocked because the age falls between birthdays.

sources.title: Government of Yukon, Get a driver's licence (archive.org snapshot of 13 November 2025)
sources.said: New drivers must complete the Graduated Driver Licensing Program to get a Yukon driver's licence. You must: be at least 15 years of age ... You'll be in the learner stage for a minimum of 6 months. ... To be able to take your road test you must: be at least 16 years old; have had your learner’s licence for 6 months; ... Once you pass the road test, you'll be issued a novice licence. ... You'll need to be in the novice stage for at least 18 months before you're able to apply for a full class licence.
